finding.claim: deleteAccount calls canDelete(u, a) but discards the boolean result, so no authorization is enforced. Any authenticated user can delete any account. The sibling closeAccount correctly uses assertCanDelete, which shows the intended behavior.
finding.source: Any authenticated caller of DELETE /accounts/{id} supplying an arbitrary account id (IDOR/broken access control).
finding.sink: accounts.remove(id) at src/AccountService.java:23, which deletes the account.

trace.note: deleteAccount(User u, long id) is the handler for DELETE /accounts/{id}; id is attacker-controlled
Account is looked up by the supplied id with no ownership scoping
canDelete(u, a) returns a boolean that is ignored, and no exception is thrown on denial

finding.guards_checked: canDelete (lines 9-11) is correct but is never enforced on this path. assertCanDelete is used only in closeAccount. No other middleware, annotations or checks are visible in the repo. The only source file is AccountService.java. If the id is not found, a is null, and canDelete would throw an NPE, but the result would still be ignored when the account exists.

verdict.guard_found: none effective: canDelete (src/AccountService.java:9-11) returns a boolean that is discarded at line 22; assertCanDelete (13-17) throws but is only called in closeAccount (line 29). No annotations or middleware exist in the repo.
verdict.reason: At src/AccountService.java:22 the bare call `canDelete(u, a)` discards its boolean result, so `accounts.remove(id)` at line 23 runs for any authenticated user, unlike closeAccount, which calls the throwing assertCanDelete at line 29.
